ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a common-emitter amplifier circuit. The transistor emitter is grounded; the collector is connected to +Ucc through resistor RC, and RC is labeled as 2 kΩ in the figure; the base is connected to +Ucc through resistor RB, and RB is labeled as 200 kΩ in the figure, with the static voltage U1 across RB marked. At the input end there is signal source Es, source resistance Rs=200 Ω, and a coupling capacitor connected to the base; the output is taken from the collector through a coupling capacitor and is labeled Uo. Reasoning calculation: According to the given U1=9.4 V and β=50. The base quiescent current IBQ=U1/RB=9.4 V/200 kΩ=47 μA. The emitter quiescent current IEQ=(β+1)IBQ=51×47 μA≈2.40 mA. The small-signal input resistance rbe≈300 Ω+(β+1)×26 mV/IEQ=300 Ω+51×26 mV/2.40 mA≈853 Ω. The problem asks for the voltage gain Au of the amplifier circuit from Ui to Uo, so according to the method, ignore the voltage division effect of Es and Rs from the source to the input. The common-emitter voltage gain Au=-βRC/rbe=-50×2000/853≈-117.2.

raw_record.question_text: Question: In the circuit shown in figure, it is known that the static voltage \( U_I \) across \( R_B \) is 9.4V, the transistor's \( _x0008_eta \) is 50, and the signal source voltage \( E_s \) is 10mV. Find the voltage gain \( A_u \) of the amplifier circuit.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify RB = 200 kΩ and RC = 2 kΩ in a grounded-emitter common-emitter amplifier. From the text, take U1 = 9.4 V across RB and β = 50. Compute IBQ = 9.4/200 kΩ = 47 μA, then IEQ = 51 × 47 μA ≈ 2.40 mA. Compute rbe = 300 Ω + 51 × 26 mV / 2.40 mA ≈ 853 Ω. Since the requested gain is the amplifier gain from Ui to Uo, ignore the source voltage Es and source resistor for Au. Then Au = -βRC/rbe = -50 × 2000 / 853 ≈ -117.2.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a CE amplifier with grounded emitter and collector resistor 2 kΩ. Use the text value U1 = 9.4 V across the pictured 200 kΩ RB to get IBQ = 47 μA and ICQ = βIBQ = 50 × 47 μA = 2.35 mA. Compute gm = ICQ/26 mV ≈ 0.0904 S and rπ = β/gm ≈ 553 Ω. Add the standard small-signal base spreading resistance rbb′ ≈ 300 Ω, so only the fraction rπ/(rπ+300) of Ui appears across the intrinsic base-emitter junction. Then Au = Uo/Ui = -gm × 2 kΩ × rπ/(rπ+300) ≈ -117.2.
